reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that behavioral decisions in maze navigation encode dual expectations: path-length (distance) and qualitative character (direction). These combine into a structured decision-making model where each means-object is evaluated through two dimensions—its potential to reduce travel cost and its alignment with preferred characteristics. This dual evaluation implies a composite utility function U(d, dir), which underpins both Bayesian inference in GSI and state-transition logic in GSE. The failure mode arises when either dimension becomes irrelevant or contradictory, e.g., choosing a longer but visually distinct alley due to sensory overload. The mathematical structure supports a probabilistic framework where P(m_i | d, dir) defines optimal selection behavior.
